# Season report 2026

Larkspur Community Garden · prepared for the members' meeting

This report looks back on the 2026 season: who gardened with us, what grew, where the money went, and what we would like to change next year. It is long on purpose; skim the headings and stop wherever it gets interesting.

## Summary

- **48 of 50 plots** were in use for the whole season, and the waiting list is down to six names.
- The harvest log counts **1,240 kg** of vegetables, about a fifth more than last year.
- Water use stayed flat although the summer was dry, thanks to the drip lines on the long beds.
- We ended the year with a small surplus of €410, which we suggest spending on a second wheelbarrow and new hose fittings.

## Members and plots

The garden had 71 active members this year, spread over 50 plots. Eleven households joined in spring; four left, mostly because they moved away. The raised beds by the gate were taken within a week of opening day, and two of them are now shared by neighbours who garden on alternate weekends.

| Plot type | Plots | In use | Waiting list |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Small (10 m²) | 22 | 22 | 4 |
| Standard (20 m²) | 20 | 19 | 2 |
| Raised bed (2 m²) | 8 | 7 | 0 |
| **Total** | **50** | **48** | **6** |

### Volunteer hours

Members put in 1,860 volunteer hours: compost turning, path repairs, the shed roof, and the Saturday watering rota in July and August. The rota worked well once it moved to a shared list; the paper sheet on the shed door was missed by almost everyone.

1. Compost and paths: 640 hours
2. Shed and fences: 410 hours
3. Watering rota: 520 hours
4. Events and the seed shelf: 290 hours

## Harvest

The chart shows the harvest log by month. June and August were the strongest months; the July dip matches the two weeks of heat when most beds were only watered, not picked.

![Harvest by month in kilograms, May to October](harvest-chart)

Tomatoes, courgettes and potatoes made up more than half of the weight. Beans had a good year as well. Squash was disappointing again: most plants caught mildew in August, and we suggest trying a more resistant variety rather than giving up on it.

> I came for the tomatoes and stayed for the people. The Thursday evenings by the shed were the best part of my summer.
>
> A member from plot 17

## Water

Total use was 412 m³, almost the same as in 2025, although June and July were drier. The drip lines on the long beds saved the most. The timer settings that worked best are below, in case someone has to set them up again:

```
zone 1  long beds north   05:30  25 min  Mon Wed Fri
zone 2  long beds south   05:55  25 min  Mon Wed Fri
zone 3  greenhouse        06:20  10 min  daily
pause   when rain > 4 mm in the last 24 h
```

The rain barrels by the shed filled up twice in September. They are cheap to add, and two more would cover most of the greenhouse in spring.

## Money

| Item | Income | Spending |
|---|---:|---:|
| Plot fees | €2,410 | |
| Plant sale in May | €380 | |
| Water bill | | €1,120 |
| Compost delivery | | €540 |
| Tools and repairs | | €460 |
| Insurance | | €260 |
| **Result** | | **€410 surplus** |

The plant sale was a small event but paid for itself several times over. ~~We planned to raise fees for 2027.~~ We no longer think a fee increase is needed for 2027.

## What we would like to change

- **Watering rota:** keep the shared list, and add a second person on the hottest days.
- **Squash:** try a mildew-resistant variety on two plots before planting it everywhere.
- **Tools:** buy a second wheelbarrow and new hose fittings from the surplus.
  - Label every tool with the shed number, so things find their way back.
  - Move the small hand tools to the wall rack, where they can be seen.
- **Waiting list:** offer the raised beds to people on the list first, before they are advertised.

## Thanks

Thank you to everyone who turned compost, fixed the fence after the storm, watered somebody else's beans, or simply brought cake on a Thursday. A garden like this only works because so many people look after a small part of it.

---

*Questions about this report can go to the garden team before the members' meeting. The full harvest log is pinned on the shed door.*
